issues.detail: The Greek 'τον υιον του ανθρωπου' (the Son of Man) is singular, but the Vietnamese 'Con người' (Human/People) can be interpreted as plural or a general category. More importantly, the Greek specifies 'the Son of Man' as a specific title/subject, which is slightly weakened by the generic 'Con người'.
The Vietnamese translation omits the definite article/specific status implied by 'τον υιον', making it sound like 'humans' in general rather than 'the Son of Man'.
